item.title: Trump says he is thinking about suspending federal gas tax
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he was thinking about suspending the federal gas tax as high gas and diesel prices pose a risk to his Republican Party heading into the November midterm US elections.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he was thinking about suspending the federal gas tax as high gas and diesel prices pose a risk to his Republican Party heading into the November midterm US elections . DETAILS AND QUOTES: "We're thinking about that," Trump said when asked if the federal gas tax should be suspended, without providing more details. Trump has also [USN:S0N41B038 TEXT:"previously expressed support"] for suspending the US gas tax in recent months. Trump's comments came a day after he [USN:L1N45R0NK TEXT:"signed an executive order"] to expand access to tax-exempt diesel that he unveiled from a rally stage in Nebraska. High gas and diesel prices are a risk to Trump ahead of the midterm elections in which control of Congress is at stake. Republicans currently hold a narrow majority in the Senate and House of Representatives. Waiving the 18.4-cent federal gasoline tax requires Congress to pass legislation. Fuel prices have risen in response to the US-Israeli war on Iran and the Russian invasion of Ukraine , with the conflicts having led to attacks on refineries in the Middle East and Russia. Trump's approval rating has held at [USN:L6N45R122 TEXT:"a record low"] 32% in recent days, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday, with Americans most concerned about the high cost of living, spurred by soaring gasoline and diesel prices.

item.title: 再送-加州共和党員からも批判、トランプ氏がイランによるロスなど「破壊」の可能性示唆
item.description:
(デートラインを６日に修正しました。)
Steve Gorman Bo Erickson
[ロサンゼルス ６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
(デートラインを６日に修正しました。)

Steve Gorman　Bo Erickson

[ロサンゼルス ６日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領が、ロサンゼルスやサンディエゴなどの米主要都市がイランによって「破壊」され得ると発言したことを受け、カリフォルニア州の民主党指導者らに加え、一部共和党員からも批判の声が上がっている。

トランプ大統領は５日、ネブラスカ州で開いた集会で、イランとの戦争に伴うエネルギー価格などの高騰について「小さな代償」だとして自身の政策を擁護。ロサンゼルスやサンディエゴを引き合いに出し、「彼らは都市を壊滅させることもできる」とし、経済的犠牲を「世界と米国の安全を守るための代償としては小さいものだ」と述べた。

また、イランとの戦争は「実質的にはほぼ終わっている」とした上で、「間もなく終わるだろうし、いずれにせよ終わるだろう」とした。

民主党の牙城であるカリフォルニア州の都市に言及した発言を受け、同州のニューサム知事（民主）はＸへの投稿で、「カリフォルニアを占領するために州兵と海兵隊を派遣した後、今度は外国の敵がロサンゼルスとサンディエゴを『破壊すべきだ』と言っている」と批判。「トランプ大統領は常軌を逸しており、危険だ」と非難した。

ロサンゼルスのバス市長（民主）も声明で、トランプ大統領の発言は「われわれの安全を脅かしかねない」と述べた。

１１月の中間選挙の下院選に出馬している共和党のデズモンド候補はＸへの投稿で、「トランプ大統領の発言に断固として反対する。米国はイランに立ち向かい、国益を守らなければならない。しかし、最高司令官の第一の責務は米国民と祖国を守ることだ」と述べた。

共和党と連携する無所属のカイリー下院議員も声明で、トランプ氏の発言は建設的ではないとの見方を示した。

ホワイトハウスのチャン広報部長はこうした批判を一蹴。ソーシャルメディアへの投稿で、「トランプ大統領の発言を巡るメディアの過剰反応は現実に基づいていない。大統領は、核武装したイランを阻止していなければ、米都市が脅威にさらされていたと明確にしたのだ」と述べた。

item.title: Anthropic opens its most powerful AI models to more security teams
item.description: Anthropic is expanding a program that allows vetted cybersecurity professionals to test its most powerful AI models with fewer safeguards, after its Project Glasswing initiative helped uncover more than 100,000 software vulnerabilities this year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic is expanding a program that allows vetted cybersecurity professionals to test its most powerful AI models with fewer safeguards, after its Project Glasswing initiative helped uncover more than 100,000 software vulnerabilities this year. Its partners under Glasswing, an initiative aimed at securing the world's most critical software, found at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities between April and July. Anthropic's own open-source scanning found 5,500 more between April and October. More than 33,000 have so far been rated critical or high severity. Anthropic said the figures are likely an undercount and expects the true impact to be at least five times higher, as the data comes from a survey of a limited number of partners. The revamped Cyber Verification Program, or CVP, announced on Tuesday combines two programs Anthropic has run for the past six months. The first, Glasswing, gave organizations securing critical software access to Claude Mythos, Anthropic's most cyber-capable family of models. The second, the original CVP, gave vetted security teams reduced safeguards on Claude Opus and Sonnet models. The company's April unveiling of Claude Mythos Preview raised fears that AI could hack software before it had been secured. The new program has three tiers, each with its own verification requirements and security controls. All three include access to Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Mythos 5.1 and future models. The Defense tier covers work such as incident response and malware analysis. Security teams, critical infrastructure operators, open-source maintainers and researchers with a record of reported vulnerabilities can apply. The Red Team tier adds authorized penetration testing and red-teaming, but only organizations can apply. The Specialized tier has the fewest restrictions and is reserved for a small group of organizations authorized to test safety-critical systems such as power grids, flight systems and interbank transfer infrastructure. Anthropic vets each member together with the US government, and existing Glasswing members will move into this tier.

item.title: 'I'm getting fed up': early US midterm voters line up before dawn in Ohio
item.description: Voters started lining up while it was still dark on Tuesday morning at the Medina County Board of Elections as early voting began in Ohio, a state that looms large in the nationwide campaigns between Republicans and Democrats battling for control of the US Congress.
item.dc:creator: Richard Cowan
item.content:encoded: Voters started lining up while it was still dark on Tuesday morning at the Medina County Board of Elections as early voting began in Ohio, a state that looms large in the nationwide campaigns between Republicans and Democrats battling for control of the US Congress. By the time polling in the northeast Ohio county closed for the day, Democrats' turnout eclipsed that of Republicans' in a possible early sign that they are more motivated to vote this year. Though turnout is typically higher in presidential elections, which are run every four years, this year's midterm voters in Ohio have a say in one key US Senate race and two for the US House of Representatives that are seen as "toss-ups," according to the Cook Political Report. Registered Republicans, Democrats and independents interviewed by Reuters all shared similar frustrations: they are exhausted by political ads they see as deceptive and mean, they hate the US war with Iran and they really hate the inflation that they believe has become chronic. Nobody said they expected things to improved any time soon. The third person in line waiting for polling to open at 8 a.m. (1200 GMT) was Eddie St. John, 83, a retiree from the town of Wadsworth. Asked what he most wanted to see fixed as a result of the election, which ends on November 3, St. John said, "Mostly it's our economy. It sucks." "You can't afford nothing anymore. Everything's so high. Gas is getting worse all the time," he said, adding, "This guy in office now he promises this. He promises that... (but) nothing's coming down." "This guy," St. John said, is President Donald Trump, who isn't on the ballot but whom the voter said he blames more than political parties. INFLATION, WAR ON BALLOT The party in power usually suffers in midterm elections. With Republicans holding the White House and both chambers of [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"Congress at a time when Trump's approval rating"] is at a record-low 32%, Democrats are feeling increasingly competitive. Political analysts will be watching closely what unfolds in Ohio, as Trump has been a dominant force, especially among blue-collar workers who used to align with the Democratic Party. But with inflation running at around 3.4%, there is deep discontent over rising food, energy and housing costs. The US war with Iran, launched by Trump on February 28 for reasons that critics say he has not clearly articulated, also has voters worried that it will become yet another "forever war." Troy Flohr, 59, a retired policeman with the Medina County Sheriff, complained about the array of campaign ads that he said were riddled with "half-truths." Standing just feet away from a voting booth, Flohr said he usually backs Republicans but was still undecided whether to vote to reelect Republican Representative Max Miller for a third term. "I tend to like the rest of them" running as Republicans on this year's ballot, Flohr added. He said his nephew is serving in the US Army and stationed in the Middle East. Without mentioning Trump by name, he said, "I'm tired of him saying the war's going to end in two weeks, the war's going to end next month...I'm getting fed up with that." Yet Flohr said he would "probably" vote for Trump again given the chance. "I don't like where the Democrat Party has gone. I'm going to leave the rest of that comment alone," he said when asked to elaborate. INDEPENDENTS Trump won Ohio and the state's 17 electoral votes handily in 2016, 2020 and 2024, despite losing the 2020 presidential race to Democrat Joe Biden. This election could depend on whether disaffected Democrats return to their party and whether many independents turn their backs on Trump's Republicans. Medina County, seen as a swing district, has 132,345 registered voters of which 29,466 are Republicans and 15,872 Democrats. Election officials say there are 86,762 independents, who could determine whether Republicans continue their success there. Despite Republicans' advantage in registered voters in the county, 499 Democrats cast ballots on Tuesday, compared to 374 Republicans, along with 291 independents. That is a significant reversal from the first day of voting in 2024, when 369 Democrats voted, compared to 702 Republicans and 433 independents, according to county data. Even more telling is data from the 2022 midterm election, when 198 Republicans cast a vote in the first day of early voting, compared to 139 Democrats and 68 independents. SENATE SEAT IN PLAY Former Senator Sherrod Brown, a Democrat from Ohio, is trying to return to the Senate, where he served for 18 years before being defeated two years ago by Republican Senator Bernie Moreno. This time around, Brown, a populist Democrat who long railed against US trade deals with foreign competitors, is attempting to unseat Republican Jon Husted in a special election with the winner holding the seat through 2028. Political analysts see the race between Husted and Brown as a toss-up. With Republicans currently holding a 53-47 majority in the Senate, Democrats are hoping for a net gain of at least four seats, including in Ohio, in order to control the chamber. CLOSE HOUSE RACES Meanwhile, two neck-and-neck US House races could help determine next year's majority in that chamber, which Republicans currently hold with a 218-214 margin. One independent is aligned with Republicans and there are two vacancies that will be filled in the midterm elections. In the 7th congressional district, which includes Medina, just south of Cleveland, incumbent Miller is seen facing a tough challenge from Democrat Brian Poindexter. While Miller has raised far more funds than his Democratic opponent and has Trump's endorsement in a Republican-leaning district, his campaign has been hit by allegations of domestic violence, which he denies. Poindexter is a labor union ironworker and member of a suburban city council. Meanwhile, in Ohio's 9th congressional district that covers most of northwest Ohio and hugs the shores of Lake Erie, Democratic Representative Marcy Kaptur, a moderate who was first elected in 1982, is battling in another toss-up race against Republican challenger Derek Merrin, who nearly defeated her in 2024. Annie Wild, 64, a retired public school teacher, said she will vote for all Democrats on the ballot. She also said since the early days of Trump's second term she has begun to see some of the president's supporters saying they are abandoning him. But that is not coming from the voters she called "MAGA." "I've lost friends that I've had for 50 years," she said of some Trump supporters, because of the gulf between them.

item.title: Bellingham hails Kane as England's greatest after milestone appearance
item.description: Jude Bellingham hailed teammate Harry Kane as England's greatest-ever player after the captain marked his record-equalling 125th appearance by scoring two goals and creating another in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win over the Czech Republic.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jude Bellingham hailed teammate Harry Kane as England's greatest-ever player after the captain marked his record-equalling 125th appearance by scoring two goals and creating another in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win over the Czech Republic. Kane drew level with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton as England's most-capped men's player and celebrated the milestone by taking his tally to 91 international goals in front of an appreciative home crowd at Wembley. "First and foremost he is an unbelievable human being, as a captain and a man," Bellingham told ITV. "He is the best England player to ever wear the shirt and it is an honour to play with him. He is pretty unmatched. He is scoring goals for fun, he goes deep and he gets tackles in. He is only getting better." Kane helped create England's opener with a cross that was turned into his own net by Czech defender Vladimir Coufal before adding two goals of his own, prompting manager Thomas Tuchel to pay tribute to his striker's consistency. "It's what he does," Tuchel said. "I don't take it for granted, it's just exceptional every single match." Kane's latest milestone came at the stadium where his England journey began more than 11 years ago. The Bayern Munich striker made an instant impact on his 2015 debut when he came off the bench against Lithuania in a European Championship qualifier and scored 79 seconds later. "It's always special, even just walking out now and seeing the stadium, just the excitement of what's to come," Kane said before kickoff. "I try and never take it for granted. It's obviously a special night tonight, but as always, we've got to focus on the job." Kane, who also rattled a shot off the crossbar on Tuesday, has become one of the defining figures of the national team, breaking Wayne Rooney's scoring record and surpassing him as England's most-capped outfield player at the World Cup earlier this year. KANE CLOSES IN ON CENTURY The 33-year-old also broke Gary Lineker's England men's World Cup scoring record this past summer, drawing level on 10 with a double against Croatia, then moving clear with a goal against Panama. By the end of the tournament, Kane had extended the record to 14 World Cup goals. He also holds the England record for major tournament appearances with 36, goals at major tournaments (21), major tournament games as captain (32) and goals at Wembley (31). And now, he is nine shy of the elusive 100-goal mark that only three male players have reached in history in Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo, Argentina great Lionel Messi and Ali Daei of Iran. "He's at the level where tonight, this is what we expect of him: two, three goals, whatever. The guy's a machine," former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said on ITV's broadcast. "That desire to score goals, it's fantastic." "The hardest people to impress sometimes are your teammates and they all speak so highly of him, talk about how brilliant he is on the pitch, he's also got a good attitude ... he deserves everything that comes his way." Shilton, whose cap record has stood since 1990, posted a congratulatory message on X. "You will go on and beat (the record) in November, I'm sure of that, and maybe go on and set a record that will never be beaten," he said in a video. "Because you're still going strong, Harry, still playing well and scoring goals, and I know how much dedication and hard work you've actually put into achieving this."

item.title: 米ＦＲＢ、インフレ抑制へ追加利上げ必要＝カンザスシティー連銀総裁
item.description: [ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 米カンザスシティー地区連銀のシュミッド総裁は６日、長期金利の上昇が一部の経済活...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ＦＲＢ、インフレ抑制へ追加利上げ必要＝カンザスシティー連銀総裁 3:40 配信

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）ビル。2025年9月撮影。REUTERS/Ken Cedeno

[ワシントン　６日　ロイター] - 米カンザスシティー地区連銀のシュミッド総裁は６日、長期金利の上昇が一部の経済活動の重しになっているとしても、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）はインフレ抑制のために追加利上げを実施する必要があるとの考えを示した。

シュミッド氏はオクラホマ州で開催された地域経済イベントで、債券利回りの上昇が借り入れコストを押し上げ、「特定のセクターで若干軟調さがみられるかもしれないが、われわれは短期金利に注目しており、個人的にはまだやるべきことがあると考えている」と述べた。

同総裁は今年の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で投票権を持っていない。

item.title: 米追加利上げの是非、インフレ押し上げショックの展開次第＝ＳＦ連銀総裁
item.description: [６日 ロイター] - 米サンフランシスコ地区連銀のデイリー総裁は６日、今後の追加利上げの是非について、インフレを押し...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米追加利上げの是非、インフレ押し上げショックの展開次第＝ＳＦ連銀総裁 3:03 配信

米サンフランシスコ地区連銀のデイリー総裁。同地区連銀ビルで４月撮影。REUTERS/Carlos Barria

[６日　ロイター] - 米サンフランシスコ地区連銀のデイリー総裁は６日、今後の追加利上げの是非について、インフレを押し上げてきたショックが収束に向かうのか、逆にショックが相互に重なり合って持続するのかに大きく左右されるとの考えを示した。

デイリー総裁はアクシオスとのインタビューで、９月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）ではインフレリスクの高まりを受けて利上げを支持したと説明。その上で「われわれが経験してきたショック、つまり関税措置、中東紛争に伴う原油価格の急騰、そしてＡＩ（人工知能）が一時的な影響しか及ぼさない従来型のショックであると判明すれば、追加利上げは不要かもしれない。私は依然としてその可能性を一定程度想定している」と語った。

さらに「ただ、これらのショックが互いに相乗効果を生むか、あるいはわれわれの予想より長引くのであれば、もし第２弾の関税交渉が行われてさらなる関税が課されれば、最初のショックに第２のショックが重なることになる。そうなればこれらのショックが影響を及ぼす期間が長引くことになるだろう」と述べた。

デイリー氏は、ＡＩ関連の半導体需要が高まっており、これがインフレ圧力を押し上げ、ショックの影響をより長期化させる可能性があるとの見方も示した。

同総裁は今年のＦＯＭＣで投票権は持っていない。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：米政府、借り入れコスト抑制へ選択肢狭まる　歳出削減以外ならインフレ加速も 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：米長期金利5％接近で株式市場に警戒感、決算後はマクロ要因に注目 焦点：ベセント氏発言で強まる日銀9月利上げ観測、米国の影響力拡大に懸念も アングル：米国債「ツイスト・スティープ化」、ＦＲＢの信認巡る懸念反映か 最終更新: 10/7(水) 3:03 ロイター

item.title: Yemeni government fighters shown driving vehicles over Houthi opponents
item.description: Video posted by government forces in Yemen showed them driving armoured cars over Houthi fighters as they recaptured areas around the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait from the Iran-backed group on Monday in a deadly new phase of the fragmented country's war.
item.dc:creator: Edward Carron
item.content:encoded: Video posted by government forces in Yemen showed them driving armoured cars over Houthi fighters as they recaptured areas around the vital [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] from the Iran-backed group on Monday in a deadly new phase of the fragmented country's war. The videos gave a glimpse into the brutal closing stages of a pitched battle for control of territory near the strait that the Houthis had captured last month. The Houthi advance sent shockwaves through the oil market and pushed up petrol and diesel prices worldwide. Fighting continued near Bab el-Mandeb on Tuesday as Saudi-backed government forces battled to consolidate [USN:L1N45R06H TEXT:"Monday's counter-attack"], besieging Houthi fighters at a military camp near the strait and pushing into hills to the east, Yemeni military sources said. The videos, verified by Reuters and filmed from inside the armoured vehicles, showed them striking fighters with their vehicles. Some were armed and some were walking or running. However, others were unarmed and some were sitting, lying or crouching on the sandy shore and made no move to evade the oncoming vehicle as they were run over. At one point, a vehicle hits a man, running and unarmed, and another crouching on the ground. It then loops back to drive over two men, both with their hands up and unarmed. Shooting can be heard during the video and at one point the vehicle's windscreen is cracked by a gunshot. A Houthi statement decried the videos as proof of war crimes, saying they showed "the true nature of the Saudi regime and the forces it has mobilised from extremist factions". Asil al-Saqladi, spokesperson for the Giants Brigade — the main Yemeni government force involved in the fighting at Bab el-Mandeb this week — said the force was conducting an investigation into the incident. He added that the brigade had been misled into believing that the Houthi fighters there were surrendering but that some of them had then fired on the government force. The Saudi-led coalition backing the government forces in Yemen did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the videos or the Houthi accusations of war crimes. The Homeland Shield Forces, a significant formation in the Yemeni government's military coalition, did not comment directly on the videos but issued a directive on Tuesday urging troops to treat prisoners well and adhere to religious, ethical and legal standards. Rights groups have previously accused the Houthis of war crimes, including sniper and shelling attacks on civilian targets, seizures of aid, abuse of prisoners and use of child soldiers. The group has denied war crimes. 'TURNING POINT' Reuters has not been able to independently verify the extent of government gains and the Houthis denied they had lost ground, saying the government claims of advances were baseless. Intense fighting meanwhile continued around Yemen's third-largest city of Taiz, where Houthi gains in a mountain district have in recent days cut off a main road to Aden, leaving government forces encircled. Yemen's [USN:L6N3Y307N TEXT:"civil war"] pits the Houthis against an uneasy coalition of sometimes rival military forces under the internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia and its allies. The renewed clashes have added a new front to the Iran-US conflict , with the [USN:L6N45308G TEXT:"US rebuffing"] Saudi requests for military help to reverse Houthi gains on the Red Sea coast near Bab el-Mandeb last month and end the group's missile and drone attacks on their territory. "The operation itself is significant because it's a turning point in the trajectory of the conflict between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition," said Ahmed Nagi, Yemen analyst at International Crisis Group. "The biggest test will be when they move towards the mountains," he added. RELIGIOUS AND REGIONAL FAULTLINES The Giants Brigade is a southern military formation originally formed by students at ultra-conservative Sunni Muslim religious colleges. That background gives both a religious and regional edge to their enmity with the Houthis, who originate in north Yemen and belong to the Zaydi school of Shi'ite Islam. The Giants have themselves fractured this year, splitting between factions backed by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, illustrating the internal divisions that have long beset the Yemeni government's efforts to fight the Houthis. As well as further squeezing global trade routes after Iran's disruption of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the conflagration in Yemen has brought the conflict more directly to Saudi Arabia, a US ally. The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi infrastructure, including airports, oil refineries and pipelines. Residents of the Saudi capital Riyadh reported hearing booms overnight and two of the kingdom's [USN:L1N45S0BG TEXT:"southern airports"] were targeted. Saudi Arabia's intervention in the latest wave of fighting included intense air strikes on Houthi forces on Monday as the Giants Brigade advanced along the flat coastal strip towards Bab el-Mandeb.

item.title: ロシアが「大規模攻撃」準備、防衛支援巡る各国対応重要＝ゼレンスキー氏
item.description: [６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[６日　ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は６日、最新の情報分析で、ロシアがウクライナに対する「大規模な攻撃」を準備していることが示されていると述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏は恒例の夜のビデオ演説で「ロシアが大規模な攻撃を準備していることが最新の情報分析で示されている」と述べた。その上で「ウクライナの情報機関と空軍は利用可能な防空手段が許す限りの対応する用意ができている」とし、ウクライナが必要とする防衛能力を保有し、それを提供できる各国首脳の対応が極めて重要になっているとの認識を示した。

item.title: 米中ロ首脳会談に関心、 11月ＡＰＥＣ首脳会議で ＝ロシア大統領補佐官
item.description: [モスクワ ６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ　６日　ロイター] - ロシアのウシャコフ大統領補佐官は６日、中国で１１月に開かれるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議に合わせ、プーチン大統領、トランプ米大統領、中国の習近平国家主席による３者会談が実現する可能性について、ロシアとして関心を持っていると述べた。

ウシャコフ氏は、この構想は初期段階にあり、詳細はまだ調整されていないとした上で、ＡＰＥＣ首脳会議の議長国を務める中国が今後議題を提示するとし、３カ国首脳による会談の機会が設けられる可能性があるとの見方を示した。

ＡＰＥＣ首脳会議は１１月１８─１９日に開かれる。

ウシャコフ氏はこのほか、イランのペゼシュキアン大統領が９日にトルクメニスタンで開かれる旧ソ連諸国首脳会議に出席し、その際にプーチン大統領と会談すると明らかにした。

FAST

LONDON/SEOUL, Oct 6 : Russia imported more than 176,000 tons of petroleum products from South Korean ports in July and August, easing the impact of a fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, Ukraine's top sanctions official said on Tuesday. The supplies from South Korea made up 31 per cent of Russian fuel imports in August, according to the official, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, citing what he said were reports that tankers, including ones under Western sanctions, were used for the deliveries. "These shipments began precisely when Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries were reducing processing volumes and creating a fuel shortage within Russia," Vlasiuk, presidential commissioner for Ukrainian sanctions policy, wrote on Facebook. His comments come amid a diplomatic row between Seoul and Kyiv that erupted last month when President Volodymyr Zelenskiy announced the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea, a step that Seoul says was meant to stay secret.

Ukraine has used long-range drones to attack Russian oil refineries and depots this year in what Kyiv has described as an effort to impose greater costs on its enemy, with no end in sight more than four years since Russia's full-scale invasion. The strikes prompted Russia to impose a ban on diesel and gasoline exports, while restricting fuel purchases in some regions hit hard by the fuel crunch. "In effect, imports from South Korea helped Russia offset the impact of losing its own refining capacity," Vlasiuk said, citing "available data" and "reports" as sources in his post. Earlier on Tuesday, the Guardian reported that it had analysed port records and ship-tracking data, determining that the volumes were loaded at South Korean ports onto seven tankers, some of which are under UK and EU sanctions. Vlasiuk provided the same figures as those in the Guardian. "This stands in stark contrast to the sanctions policy South Korea adopted following the start of the full-scale invasion," Vlasiuk said. In response to the Guardian article, South Korea's Foreign Ministry said "the Korean government supports and actively participates in global efforts to end the war in Ukraine and achieve peaceful recovery". It said that its government was strictly enforcing export controls against Russia by expanding the scope beyond strategic items to include "non-strategic items ... that carry a high risk of diversion for military use." Relations between South Korea and Ukraine have been under strain for weeks. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified measures against Ukraine on Friday unless Kyiv acknowledged a confidentiality agreement that Seoul says covered the transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers. Seoul has said it wants an apology. Ukraine denies there was a confidentiality agreement, but its foreign minister has said that Kyiv wants to mend ties with South Korea.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Cardinals LT Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps) out for season
item.description: Arizona Cardinals placed starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. on injured reserve for the third straight year and he will miss the remainder of the season with a torn left biceps, head coach Mike LaFleur announced Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Arizona Cardinals placed starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. on injured reserve for the third straight year and he will miss the remainder of the season with a torn left biceps, head coach Mike LaFleur announced Tuesday. Johnson sustained the injury in the fourth quarter of Arizona's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday. "I don't know exactly when (surgery is) going to happen, but it's going to happen soon to get the process going. I know I was quick on that," LaFleur said. "I feel for him -- just all these guys. It sucks for him, first and foremost. It sucks obviously for the Arizona Cardinals, our offense, this team. But it's NFL football -- here we are in October and the show goes on." Rookie Jayden Williams, who was a seventh-round pick out of Mississippi, replaced Johnson on Sunday. Arizona also placed tight end Hunter Long (right knee) on injured reserve, signed tight end Tegan Quitoriano from the practice squad to the active roster and signed offensive tackle Jedrick Wills Jr. from the Buffalo Bills' practice squad to the team's active roster. In other moves, tight end Kenny Yeboah, offensive lineman Austin Deculus and safety Mark Perry were signed to the practice squad and offensive lineman Vershon Lee and cornerback D'Shawn Jamison were released from the practice squad. Johnson, 25, started all four of his games this season and all 47 in which he has played since being selected by the Cardinals with the sixth overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Ohio State. Wills, 27, played in 58 regular-season games (57 starts) and two playoff games (both starts) for the Cleveland Browns from 2020-24. He injured his knee in a 2023 game against the Cardinals, played in just five games in 2024 and missed the entire 2025 season. Wills signed with the Chicago Bears in March and, after dealing with a back issue, was released on Aug. 30. He signed with the Bills on Sept. 1. Cleveland selected Wills with the 10th overall pick of the 2020 NFL Draft out of Alabama. Long, 28, has two receptions on two targets for 15 yards in four games as a reserve this season. He has played on 33% of the offensive snaps (91) and 53% of special teams snaps (57). He has 22 career receptions for 168 yards and two touchdowns in 50 games (eight starts) for the Miami Dolphins (2021-22), Los Angeles Rams (2023-24), Jacksonville Jaguars (2025) and Cardinals. Arizona obtained him and a 2028 seventh-round pick in an Aug. 30 trade with the Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-round selection. Miami picked Long in the third round of the 2021 draft out of Boston College. The Cardinals (1-3) host the Lions (2-2) on Sunday in Glendale, Ariz. --Field Level Media

item.title: リトアニア、核兵器禁止条項撤廃へ 議会で第1回採決通過
item.description: ［ビリニュス ６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ビリニュス　６日　ロイター］ - リトアニア議会は６日、核兵器を禁じる憲法の条項撤廃提案について、１回目の投票で可決した。議員１４１のうち１０６人が賛成票を投じ、可決に必要な３分の２以上の賛成を確保した。条項撤廃には２回目の投票でも３分の２以上の賛成が必要となり、来年１月１２日に採決が予定されている。

禁止条項はリトアニアが旧ソ連から独立して以降、３０年以上維持されてきた。ロシアによるウクライナへの全面侵攻などを経て、バルト３国などの安全保障上の前提が変化していることが示された形となった。

リトアニアのナウセーダ大統領は、国内に核兵器を配備する計画は当面ないものの、条項撤廃により安全保障環境が変化した場合には対応できるようになると説明。各党が禁止条項の撤廃案で合意したと述べていた。ナウセーダ氏は７月、リトアニアが引き続き核拡散防止条約（ＮＰＴ）の締約国にとどまることも表明している。

item.title: Thousands of European wind and solar power systems exposed online, Dutch researchers say
item.description: Thousands of administrative systems at wind and solar power parks in Europe are exposed to the internet, potentially giving attackers access to interfaces that can stop turbines and raising the risk of sabotage, Dutch researchers warned on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie van den Berg, Toby Sterling
item.content:encoded: Thousands of administrative systems at wind and solar power parks in Europe are exposed to the internet, potentially giving attackers access to interfaces that can stop turbines and raising the risk of sabotage, Dutch researchers warned on Tuesday. The exposed systems included administrative and login interfaces as well as operational interfaces showing data and controls. However, one of the researchers, Soufian El Yadmani, from internet-scanning company Modat, told Reuters that researchers believed full control would have been possible in the case of around 181 sites. One turbine's web page showed live data, "Start, Stop and Reset" buttons and the turbine's location, the research said. Some systems controlled several turbines or a whole farm. "What we can map in hours, an attacker can map in hours too," the report said. The researchers urged operators to take admin interfaces off the internet immediately. SPANISH SOLAR, GERMAN WIND MOST EXPOSED The findings come amid [USN:L8N45F1L2 TEXT:"concerns about Europe's critical infrastructure,"] which has faced suspected sabotage and cyberattacks frequently attributed by Western governments to Russia since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russia denies any involvement. Last month, Dutch intelligence agencies, police and prosecutors warned that artificial intelligence was accelerating the threat. El Yadmani and Bouke van Laethem of the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre presented their findings on Tuesday at the ONE Conference in The Hague. Turbines or arrays closely linked to public infrastructure were a special concern, El Yadmani said. "If you can turn off the energy within the city or the airport, imagine that at a larger scale." Using machine learning to sort and cluster data, the pair said they identified 8,547 internet-facing systems they could link to at specific solar parks (7,942) and wind farms (605) in 35 European countries, which should not have been exposed to the internet. Most of the systems found were admin pages with login screens. Spain had the most exposed solar systems, with 2,766, followed by Greece with 1,860, they said. Germany has Europe's most installed solar capacity, and 672 exposed solar systems. However it had the most exposed wind systems with 212, with Italy close behind at 192. The researchers said the rankings partly reflected where they had been able to link systems to specific sites. The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity could not immediately comment. Authorities in Germany, Italy and Spain did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The report listed among its sources the Polish cybersecurity team CERT Polska's analysis of a [USN:L6N3YV10T TEXT:"December 2025 attack"] on 30 wind and solar sites in Poland, an example of the potential threat.

item.title: 巨大メディア「スカイダンス」誕生、パラマウントのワーナー買収完了
item.description:
Anzar Mehraj Harshita Mary Varghese
[６日 ロイター] - 米メディア大手パラマウ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
巨大メディア「スカイダンス」誕生、パラマウントのワーナー買収完了 10/6 23:48 配信

米カリフォルニア州ロサンゼルスのパラマウント・スタジオで９月撮影。REUTERS/Daniel Cole

Anzar Mehraj　Harshita Mary Varghese

[６日　ロイター] - 米メディア大手パラマウント・スカイダンスは６日、ワーナー・ブラザース・ディスカバリー（ＷＢＤ）を買収する１１００億ドル規模の大型取引が完了したと発表した。これにより、新会社「スカイダンス」が誕生し、デービッド・エリソン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が世界最大級のエンターテインメント企業を率いることになる。

統合後の新会社「スカイダンス」の株式は６日、ナスダックからニューヨーク証券取引所に移管され、「SKYD」のティッカーシンボルで取引が開始された。

人気映画シリーズ「ミッション：インポッシブル」や「ハリー・ポッター」などを手がけるスタジオに、ＣＢＳニュース、ＣＮＮニュース、「パラマウント＋（プラス）」、「ＨＢＯマックス」などの主要なテレビや動画配信サービスが統合され、映画、テレビ、ニュースを網羅する広範なエンターテインメント企業が誕生する。

トランプ米大統領は、記者団から買収完了について質問され、「素晴らしい企業になるだろう」とし、「素晴らしい合併だ」と応じた。

トランプ大統領は１期目から報道機関を批判し、最近ではＷＢＤ傘下のニュース専門局ＣＮＮを含む３社の記者らをホワイトハウスから締め出すという異例の措置を講じた。

５日発表された新会社の経営陣の詳細によると、ＣＮＮのマーク・トンプソン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）はＣＮＮの会長兼編集長として続投し、ＣＢＳニュースのバリ・ワイス編集長も現職にとどまる。これにより、ＣＮＮとＣＢＳはそれぞれ独立した編集体制を維持する見通しで、ＣＢＳのワイス氏が新会社全体のニュース部門を統括するとの懸念は後退した。

エリソンＣＥＯは、パラマウント傘下のＣＢＳニュースの報道内容をトランプ氏に有利なものにしようとしたとの批判を議員らから受けており、統合後の編集の独立性を巡る懸念が高まっていた。

また、新会社は約８００億ドルの負債を抱える見通しで、エリソン氏には配信事業の拡大、ケーブルネットワーク事業からのキャッシュフロー維持、劇場公開映画の業績改善が求められる。

調査会社モフェットナサンソンのアナリストは、同社の２０２８年の利払い・税引き・償却前利益（ＥＢＩＴＤＡ）を１６０億ドル、３０年には１９０億ドルに増加すると予想。売上高は２８年に約６７０億ドル、３０年には約７００億ドルに達すると見込む。

スカイダンスは、買収完了後の最初の２年間は年間少なくとも３０本、その後の３年間は年間３２本の映画を製作すると公約している。

エリソン氏は先週、統合後の新会社名を「スカイダンス」とした理由について、パラマウントとワーナー・ブラザースの両映画スタジオの個別のアイデンティティーが失われないようにすることが目的で、新たな企業ブランドの下に統合するものではないと説明していた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：武田薬のシャイアー買収5年、大型Ｍ＆Ａの難しさ示す コラム：ＡＩブームの恩恵受ける小型テック株、先行きは不透明 アングル：米株式取引24時間化、ウォール街では期待と慎重論が交錯 アングル：米株のテック依存、「ＩＴバブル期」上回る　市場を不安定に 焦点：過熱するＡＩ相場、収益化への懸念で市場に警戒感も 最終更新: 10/7(水) 6:09 ロイター

Euro bounces as decline in French bond yields cools debt jitters

Euro banknotes are seen in this illustration taken March 24, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

FILE PHOTO: A shopper pays for vegetables with a five-euro banknote and coins at a local market in Paris, France, September 10, 2026. REUTERS/Stephanie Lecocq/File Photo

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 6 : The euro rebounded on Tuesday and was poised for its strongest move higher in seven weeks after falling to a 17-month low on the prior day, as a pullback in French government bond yields eased fears about strain in euro zone debt markets. The euro zone's currency jumped 0.35 per cent, on track for its biggest daily gain since August 19, at $1.126. The currency had slid to its lowest since May 2025 on Monday at $1.116, following a drop of more than 1 per cent in the prior week, its fourth straight weekly decline.  The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, fell 0.32 per cent to 101.83 and was on pace for its biggest daily drop since September 3.  Bond markets around the world have seen yields climb in recent weeks due to expectations of sharp central bank rate hikes as energy prices have jumped because of the Iran war and stoked inflation, as well as concerns about government finances.

French debt has seen pressure mount as politicians struggle to curb the budget deficit ahead of a divisive election in 2027. The calling of a snap election in Spain added to the recent pressure on the euro. ENERGY PRICES EASE BOND PRESSURE An early drop in energy prices helped French bonds rally on Tuesday, with the key 10-year yield down 11.4 basis points at 4.7506 per cent. Crude prices had fallen as rising Middle Eastern crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release eased supply concern as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces staged a lightning advance on Monday to retake the coast around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait up to the city of Mocha, the government said, but prices had since rebounded to erase declines.  "Saudi-backed Yemen forces have recaptured some strategic territory from the Houthis, this has seen oil prices drop sharply," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets in New York. "In turn, this has helped drag yields down, including in France, and in Italy, where the spreads had really widened lately and so this is giving the euro a bit of a bounce." Far-right French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who leads the polls, on Tuesday increased her plans to reduce spending to €140 billion ($158 billion) from €125 billion in savings originally planned if she wins power in 2027.   The fall in the dollar helped buoy other currencies, with sterling up 0.42 per cent and on pace for its biggest daily gain since August 19, to $1.3275, after climbing to a one-week high of $1.3283. JAPAN SIGNALS RATE RISE READINESS The yen was an exception, with the dollar up 0.11 per cent to 158.08 against the Japanese currency.  The Bank of Japan may signal this month that underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2 per cent target, three people familiar with its thinking said, highlighting its readiness to raise interest rates again in the coming months. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said it was becoming more important to anchor underlying inflation around the central bank's 2 per cent target, signaling a preparedness to keep raising interest rates to blunt the risk of too-high inflation. The US dollar's recent strength has come even as expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike at the central bank's policy meeting later this month have retreated in the wake of weaker-than-expected US jobs data and comments from some Fed officials. However, markets are still anticipating more rate hikes later in the year and next year.  The gains for the dollar in September were partly due to the greater exposure of US equities to technology and AI, said Goldman Sachs analysts in a note, along with the recent outperformance of US growth. But the firm is cautious on the prospects for near-term dollar strength, citing stretched positioning in several major pairs and the recent Fed communication emphasizing a patient approach to policy tightening.  In contrast to the recent call for patience from some Fed officials, Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said on Tuesday that the central bank still needs to raise its policy rate further to lower inflation, even if higher long-term yields are weighing on activity in some parts of the economy.  The chance of a hike of at least 25 basis points in October stands at about 19 per cent, from about 51 per cent a week ago, according to CME FedWatch, but markets are pricing in an 86 per cent chance for a hike at the December meeting.

Source: Reuters

Google fights £1 billion UK lawsuit over app store fees in latest Big Tech case

FILE PHOTO: The Google logo is seen outside the company's offices in London, Britain, June 24, 2025. REUTERS/Carlos Jasso/File Photo

FAST

LONDON, Oct 6 : Google was accused of abusing its dominance to levy excessive commissions on app developers, as a mass consumer lawsuit worth over £1 billion ($1.33 billion) began in London on Tuesday. The case — brought on behalf of around 20 million consumers who bought apps through Google's Play Store, or paid for in-app purchases and subscriptions between 2015 and this July — is the latest brought in Britain against Big Tech. Lawyers representing consumer advocate Liz Coll, who is leading the claim, say Google used its dominant position to charge commissions of up to 30 per cent on purchases of apps through its Play Store, as well as on in-app purchases and subscriptions. They argue that those excessive commissions were passed on by app developers to consumers, citing as an example that when Google sold YouTube Premium through Apple's App Store it also decided to pass on the commission it was charged.

But Google's parent Alphabet is fighting the lawsuit, which a spokesperson said ignores the degree of choice the Android platform gives consumers and that it charges "some of the lowest fees in the market". The tech giant's lawyers, who said Coll's case was unfounded, argued the Play Store "faces strong competitive constraints both on the developer and consumer sides", including from Apple's App Store and other alternative platforms. The trial at London's Competition Appeal Tribunal follows similar cases against Apple and Sony over their App Store and PlayStation Store, both of which cited commissions of up to 30 per cent. Coll's case also comes after years of regulatory scrutiny and litigation over Google's app store practices, including a long-running battle with "Fortnite" maker Epic Games, whose London lawsuit was due to be heard alongside Coll's. In March, Google and Epic reached a worldwide settlement under which Google said it would expand billing options and cut developer fees. Last month, Google also settled another lawsuit for £260 million, which was brought on behalf of app developers, without making any admission of liability or wrongdoing. ($1 = 0.7536 pounds)

item.title: ＩＭＦ、ヘッジファンドの存在感拡大 監視強化を要請
item.description:
Pete Schroeder
[ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は６日、ヘッジファンドは過去１...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＩＭＦ、ヘッジファンドの存在感拡大　監視強化を要請 10/6 23:21 配信

米ワシントンにある国際通貨基金（IMF）本部前で2018年5月撮影。REUTERS/Yuri Gripas

Pete Schroeder

[ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は６日、ヘッジファンドは過去１０年あまりで資産規模が３倍以上に拡大し、現在では市場においてますます重要な役割を担っていると指摘した。同時に、ファンドによるレバレッジの利用と全体的な不透明性が金融システムにリスクをもたらす可能性があると警告した。

ＩＭＦは６日、世界金融安定報告書の一部の公表にあわせ、この調査結果を発表した。報告書全文は１０月１３日に公表される。調査結果は以下のとおり。

• ヘッジファンドは、トレーディング、流動性、リスク移転においてますます重要な役割を担っており、ファンドの資産は２０１３年のわずか４兆ドルから２６年初頭には約１３兆ドルにまで大幅に増加している。

• ヘッジファンドの成長は主にレバレッジ、特にデリバティブを通じた合成レバレッジによってもたらされてきた。

• こうしたファンドは、特に米国債市場において、その存在感を著しく高めている。ヘッジファンドは現在、米国債市場の９％を占めており、２２年のわずか４％から大幅に増加している。

• ヘッジファンドの存在感が高まることで市場効率が向上する可能性がある一方で、特にこれらの企業がレバレッジを利用し、リスクに対する制約が少ないことから、市場が悪化した際にストレスを増幅させる可能性もある。

• ヘッジファンドは依然として「本質的に不透明」であり、リスクやエクスポージャーを正確に評価することが困難である。政策立案者は、データ不足を解消し、潜在的な脆弱性に対する同セクターのリスク監視を強化する必要がある。

item.title: IMF says hedge funds' market footprint growing, merits closer scrutiny
item.description: Hedge funds have more than tripled in size in the last decade and now play increasingly critical market roles, the International Monetary Fund said Tuesday, while warning that the funds' use of leverage and overall opacity can inject risks into the financial system.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder
item.content:encoded: Hedge funds have more than tripled in size in the last decade and now play increasingly critical market roles, the International Monetary Fund said Tuesday, while warning that the funds' use of leverage and overall opacity can inject risks into the financial system. The findings were published Tuesday by the IMF as it released a chapter of its Global Financial Stability Report, which will be released in full on Oct. 13. Here's what the group found: Hedge funds are playing an increasingly prominent role in trading, liquidity and risk transfers, as assets at the funds now stand at roughly $13 trillion in early 2026, up significantly from just $4 trillion in 2013 Hedge fund growth has primarily come through leverage, including synthetic leverage through derivatives Such funds have grown their footprint significantly in sovereign bond markets, particularly US Treasuries. Hedge funds now account for 9% of the Treasury market, compared to just 4% in 2022 While greater hedge fund presence can boost market efficiency, the IMF warned they can also amplify stress when markets deteriorate, particularly due to those firms' use of leverage and fewer constraints on risk The IMF warned that hedge funds remain "inherently opaque," making it difficult to accurately gauge their risks and exposures. It called on policymakers to close data gaps and boost risk monitoring of the sector for potential vulnerabilities

item.title: Marvell raises 2028 revenue forecast on strong AI data center demand
item.description: Marvell Technology raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast to about $20 billion on Tuesday, above Wall Street estimates, as demand for its custom data center chips grows along with a surge in AI spending.
item.dc:creator: Prathik Jayaprakash, Anhata Rooprai, Max Cherney
item.content:encoded: Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast to about $20 billion on Tuesday, above Wall Street estimates, as demand for its custom data center chips grows along with a surge in AI spending. Shares of the Santa Clara, California-based company rose about 6%, while those of rival Broadcom (AVGO.O) advanced about 4%. "It took a long time to get this company on this path and to be a technology leader," Chris Koopmans, Marvell's president and chief operating officer, said in an interview. "We have a track record of doing what we said we're going to do." Marvell outlined a strategy in 2021 centered on custom and cloud-optimized silicon — chips specifically designed for use in data centers. It has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom since then and projects it will generate $12 billion in custom chip revenue in fiscal 2029, up from a prior target of $10 billion. The company's custom chip business has become a major growth engine, with technology companies developing in-house AI processors to reduce reliance on Nvidia (NVDA.O) chips. Marvell's stock has more than tripled in value so far this year. Marvell disclosed a deal with Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) in August that could generate up to $120 billion in sales through fiscal 2033, if performance milestones are achieved. That same month, it raised its full-year revenue outlook to about $18 billion from $16.5 billion. On Tuesday, Marvell forecast fiscal 2031 revenue of $70 billion to $90 billion. At $80 billion, the midpoint of that range exceeds Wall Street estimates of $46.85 billion, according to four analysts polled by Visible Alpha. Analysts were expecting revenue of $18.2 billion for 2028, according to data compiled by LSEG.

item.title: 米8月貿易赤字、1056億ドルと25年3月以来の高水準
item.description: [ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 米商務省が６日発表した８月の貿易赤字（季節調整済み）は前月比１３．７％増の１０５６億...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米8月貿易赤字、1056億ドルと25年3月以来の高水準 10/6 22:42 配信

米カリフォルニア州ロングビーチ港沖に停泊するコンテナ船。７月撮影。REUTERS/Mario Anzuoni

[ワシントン　６日　ロイター] - 米商務省が６日発表した８月の貿易赤字（季節調整済み）は前月比１３．７％増の１０５６億ドルと、２０２５年３月以来の高水準となった。堅調な内需を背景に輸入が過去最高を記録し、ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想（１０２０億ドル）を上回った。第３・四半期も貿易が経済成長の押し下げ要因となる見通しとなった。

８月の輸入は４．３％増の４２０８億ドルと過去最高となった。モノの輸入は５．３％増の３４２２億ドル。石油を含む工業用資材・原材料が９１億ドル増加したことが押し上げ要因となった。

原油の輸入は３３億ドル増、非貨幣用金は３１億ドル増加した。資本財の輸入は、半導体やその他の産業機械がけん引し、６２億ドル増の１４６４億ドルと過去最高となった。一方、コンピューター周辺機器は１６億ドル減少した。

サービス輸入は１億ドル弱の増加にとどまり、７８５億ドルとなった。輸送サービスが小幅に増加した一方、知的財産使用料や旅行サービスは減少した。

８月の輸出は１．４％増の３１５２億ドル、モノの輸出は２．２％増の２０５７億ドルとなった。工業用資材・原材料が６３億ドル増加した。資本財の輸出は、半導体とコンピューターに押し上げられ１３億ドル増加。一方、民間航空機は１０億ドル減少した。 消費財の輸出は２２億ドル減少。医薬品が２４億ドル減少したことが響いた。

サービス輸出は１０９５億ドルと、１億ドル弱の増加にとどまった。知的財産使用料とその他ビジネスサービスが小幅に増加した一方、旅行サービスと金融サービスはともに減少した。

貿易は３四半期連続で国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）の押し下げ要因となっており、エコノミストらは第３・四半期のＧＤＰを最大２．５％ポイント押し下げる可能性があると試算している。

第３・四半期の成長率予想は概ね年率３．０％を上回っており、個人消費が輸入によるマイナス影響を相殺すると見込まれている。第２・四半期の成長率は２．２％だった。

トランプ大統領は貿易赤字の縮小に向けて輸入品に対する強硬な関税措置を講じてきたものの、赤字は逆に拡大し、メキシコ、ベトナム、マレーシアに対するモノの貿易赤字は過去最大となった。台湾、中国、欧州連合（ＥＵ）、韓国、カナダ、インドなどに対しても引き続き赤字となった。一方、ベルギーに対するモノの貿易黒字は過去最大を記録。オランダ、中南米、英国、香港、ブラジル、オーストラリア、サウジアラビアに対しても黒字を維持した。

ＦＷＤＢＯＮＤＳのチーフエコノミスト、クリストファー・ラプキー氏は「現政権の通商政策は概ね失敗に終わっており、関税措置は米国が外国製品への依存を低減することに何ら寄与していない」と指摘。「米国の労働コストは高過ぎるため、消費者が購入を検討できるほど安価な商品を国内で生産することはできない。たとえ米国の製造業者にその意思があったとしても、消費者が依存している商品を生産するための工場を国内に素早く建設することはできないだろう」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：米政府、借り入れコスト抑制へ選択肢狭まる　歳出削減以外ならインフレ加速も アングル：米移民摘発、過去最高の逮捕件数も送還難航　法的手続きや移送能力に壁 コラム：米財務省の借入拡大、債務問題の大きさに比べれば単なるノイズ 焦点：テスラ、ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」で試す規制の限界 コラム：日銀利上げの「美しいシナリオ」に弱点はないか＝上野泰也氏 最終更新: 10/7(水) 0:35 ロイター

item.title: Mali troops re-enter strategic northern town after separatists withdraw
item.description: A separatist movement in northern Mali announced on Tuesday it was carrying out "a controlled withdrawal" from a strategic town in the north, a symbolic boost to Mali's army and its Russian backers in their years-long fight against insurgents including al Qaeda-linked jihadists.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A separatist movement in northern Mali announced on Tuesday it was carrying out "a controlled withdrawal" from a strategic town in the north, a symbolic boost to Mali's army and its Russian backers in their years-long fight against insurgents including al Qaeda-linked jihadists. Malian troops were "reinforcing their presence" in the town by Tuesday night, a government statement said, adding that this would allow for "the gradual return of public administration and basic social services". The Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) took control of Kidal town six months ago in [USN:L6N41903L TEXT:"nationwide attacks"] that also killed Mali's defence minister. It had joined forces in those attacks with the regional al Qaeda affiliate, Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, known as JNIM, posing the biggest test yet to Mali's military leaders who seized power in coups in 2020 and 2021. The FLA's decision to leave Kidal came in response to airstrikes by Mali's military backed by Russian fighters, the FLA said in a statement. "The FLA specifies that this is a temporary operational measure, also intended to preserve its human and logistical capabilities intact. This methodical withdrawal from the area took place without any direct combat having yet pitted its forces against the enemy," the statement said. Mali has leaned on Russian security support for years, first from the Wagner mercenary group and then from the paramilitary group Africa Corps, which is made up of many former Wagner fighters. 'SYMBOLIC' BUT NOT DECISIVE VICTORY, ANALYST SAYS Earlier on Tuesday, Mali's military said it had launched large-scale air and ground operations in the region of Kidal. The goals of the operations included tracking down and neutralizing armed groups operating in the area, destroying their supply networks and restoring "lasting security" and free movement for people and goods, a Malian military statement said. Pro-government fighters, including Russian fighters, re-entered Kidal on Tuesday afternoon, a security source said. Malian forces and Wagner fighters retook Kidal from insurgents in November 2023, the most concrete gain from their partnership — only to lose it during the attacks in April. "A successful recapture... affirms the military-led government's authority and boosts the army's morale, particularly after several high-profile setbacks both in the north and the central regions in recent weeks," said Beverly Ochieng, associate director of Control Risks. "This is also an opportunity for Africa Corps to reprise its role as the Malian government's security guarantor after appearing to lose significant ground, including in Kidal, since April." But the change of control in Kidal is still largely "symbolic" and not "decisive" in Mali's campaign against insurgent groups, Ochieng added. A source close to the FLA leadership told Reuters that the aerial operations by Malian and Russian forces began three days ago. The source played down the significance of the FLA's withdrawal, saying it was a measure to protect lives and equipment. "For us, war is not a race against the clock," the source said.

item.title: 生活費危機、インフレ期待や貧困に長期的な影響与える＝ＩＭＦ
item.description:
Andrea Shalal
[ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は６日に公表した研究報告書で、食...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
生活費危機、インフレ期待や貧困に長期的な影響与える＝ＩＭＦ 10/6 22:27 配信

国際通貨基金（IMF）のロゴ。2024年11月撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

Andrea Shalal

[ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は６日に公表した研究報告書で、食料とエネルギー価格の急上昇は今後より頻繁に起こる可能性が高いと述べ、こうした危機はインフレ期待を長期にわたって高め、貧困を悪化させ、経済の安定を脅かすと警告した。

各国政府が物価高騰を緩和するために用いてきた３０年間の戦略を検証するとともに、生活必需品に家計のより大きな割合を費やす貧困層が経験する高いインフレ率を考慮した新たな経済モデルを提示。新しいモデルでは、標準的なインフレ指標との間に０．８％ポイントの乖離が見られ、２０２１年から２４年にかけて、以前の試算よりも２３００万人多い人々が極度の貧困ラインを下回ったことが示唆された。

研究を共同で主導したＩＭＦのエコノミスト、キアラ・マッジ氏は「要するに、生活費危機は物価安定に影響を与え、生活水準を低下させ、格差を悪化させる」と述べた。今回の研究は来週に公表される「世界経済見通し」の一部となる。

ジョージタウン大学教授で元世界銀行エコノミストのシャンタヤナン・デバラジャン氏は６日に公開されたマッジ氏とのビデオ対談の中で、原油価格の高騰、高水準の債務、借入コストの上昇、そして今年のスーパーエルニーニョ現象による影響が複合的に作用し、発展途上国は深刻な危機に直面していると指摘。「これは低所得国全体の成長率が過去最低水準にある時期に起こっている」とし、「成長率は著しく鈍化している」と語った。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：食品値下げは広がるのか、日銀判断にも影響する分岐点に アングル：イラン戦争による肥料高騰、穀物生産減少で食料危機の恐れも コラム：米だけ「異世界」のＩＭＦ会合　イラン戦争無視で政権の苦境露呈 アングル：トランプ減税、ガソリン代高騰で効果台無し アングル：イラン紛争で湾岸諸国の食料安全保障に打撃、輸入依存度は80％以上 最終更新: 10/6(火) 22:27 ロイター

item.title: New Maryland defense shipyard gets $6.6 billion commitment and Trump visit
item.description: Defense tech firm Anduril unveiled plans on Tuesday for a $3.7 billion shipyard in Maryland that is expected to generate 3,100 jobs, in a ceremony attended by President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery, Nathan Gomes, Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: Defense tech firm Anduril unveiled plans on Tuesday for a $3.7 billion shipyard in Maryland that is expected to generate 3,100 jobs, in a ceremony attended by President Donald Trump. Anduril, which was also awarded a $2.9 billion US Navy contract, said the new high-tech shipyard at Sparrows Point, Maryland, near the Port of Baltimore, would make components for the Navy's Virginia-class submarines. The investment and associated contract, together valued at up to $6.6 billion, come amid a broader push by the United States and its allies to expand arms production following Russia's invasion of Ukraine and conflicts in the Middle East. "Right here in Sparrows Point, you'll build the next generation of American submarines," Trump told a crowd of mostly students from the US Naval Academy, noting the facility will produce torpedo tubes and critical components for Virginia-class attack submarines. "American taxpayers will receive a 40% stake in the new shipyard," Trump added, although he did not indicate what the ownership mechanism would be. The US already owns four shipyards, including the Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Virginia and the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Maine, which are mostly focused on the repair and upkeep of existing ships, not construction of new vessels or components for new craft. RARE POLITICAL ALIGNMENT The project puts Trump in rare alignment with a frequent critic, Maryland Governor Wes Moore, a Democrat who is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate. Maryland and Baltimore County committed to match up to 13% of the total investment by Anduril, about $481 million, through funds that will need to be approved by local legislative bodies. In the run-up to November's congressional elections, Trump is aiming to show that his policies have bolstered jobs and manufacturing. [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"Polls have shown"] that Trump's Republicans have lost voter support, largely over cost-of-living concerns. The president has said his tariffs and industrial policy will revive US factory work, from steelmaking to shipbuilding. Anduril's location in Maryland was formerly home to a large steel mill that went through decades of financial decline and closed in bankruptcy in 2012. Trump is touring the country in a pre-election blitz, announcing or claiming credit for a range of private-sector investments and government spending initiatives he has called "goodies." END-OF-DECADE TARGET The new plant, dubbed Arsenal-2, is expected to be operational by the end of the decade. Anduril is building another facility in California to manufacture Virginia-class submarine components, and plans to expand into producing larger submarine modules and hull sections once its Baltimore shipyard becomes operational. Virginia-class submarines, which can travel at speeds exceeding 25 knots, are the Navy's latest generation of nuclear-powered attack submarines, designed for anti-submarine warfare, land-attack strikes and surveillance missions. General Dynamics' (GD.N) Electric Boat and Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII.N) jointly build them. Anduril, founded in 2017 by Palmer Luckey, is best known for its autonomous systems, drones and software built for the US military and its allies. Anduril's $1 billion [USN:L1N4070RY TEXT:"Arsenal-1 facility"] in Ohio began producing autonomous combat drones this year.

item.title: For Trump’s Treasury, the sting is in the auction ‘tail’: McGeever
item.description: US Treasury auctions are supposed to be dull, predictable, and non-newsworthy affairs. But these are not normal times, and the Trump administration now risks seeing weak debt sales make headline news.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: US Treasury auctions are supposed to be dull, predictable, and non-newsworthy affairs. But these are not normal times, and the Trump administration now risks seeing weak debt sales make headline news. The Treasury plans to sell nearly $120 billion of debt this week, the first sales outside of T-bills in two weeks: $58 billion of three-year notes on Tuesday, $39 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday, and $22 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday. These might normally be non-events, but they're under increasing scrutiny because the September 22-24 auctions were remarkably weak, particularly the five-year note auction on Sept. 23, which helped spark the biggest rise in bond yields since April last year. Yields have not come down since and have instead powered ahead to multi-decade highs across most maturities. It's worth stating that there's next to zero chance that the US would ever have a "failed" debt auction. Primary dealers – the 26 Wall Street banks and institutions currently approved by the New York Fed as Treasury market makers – will always participate. They effectively underwrite the sales, ensuring the $30 trillion US debt market – the most liquid market in the world – functions smoothly. This, in turn, keeps the entire global financial system chugging along, as well. Trillions of dollars of global debt, assets, and market derivatives use Treasuries as a reference. US government bonds are also the collateral used to lubricate the pipes of US and global financial plumbing - repo agreements, interbank lending, and funding. In short, as long as US debt is the lynchpin of the global financial system, there will always be buyers at Treasury auctions. The issue, as ever, is the price at which these sales clear. Right now, borrowing costs on the secondary market are the highest since the mid to early 2000s, so it is reasonable to assume that Treasury will pay comparably high rates on the primary market. But as the most recent auctions have shown, there is also still room for negative surprises. TOO BIG TO TAIL? The $70 billion sale of five-year notes on September 23 was one of the most alarming in recent memory. Demand as measured by the 'bid-to-cover' ratio was the lowest in nine years. Treasury ultimately sold the notes at 5.033%, which was more than three basis points above the market yield at the bidding deadline. Three basis points might not sound like a lot, but for a five-year auction, that’s extraordinary. It was the largest so-called "tail" since June 2022. To find the last time a five-year auction had a 3 bps "tail," JP Morgan analysts note, you have to go all the way back to 2011, when a brewing debt ceiling crisis would lead to a credit rating downgrade that August. Moving back to the present, concerns about the dire US fiscal outlook have pushed up long-term borrowing costs. As a result, the Trump administration is widely expected to gradually shift the weight of the Treasury’s huge borrowing requirements towards the shorter - and cheaper - end of the curve. This is why the five-year auction two weeks ago caused such alarm. "Tails" of 3 bps are common in longer bond auctions, but not in sales of debt that sit right in the so-called "belly" of the yield curve. If Treasury is being forced to pay higher premiums to shift these notes, then Houston, we have a problem. Fat auction “tails” can be a result of multiple forces, including market volatility on the day itself or more worrying fundamental issues that might erode demand over time. It's often difficult to untangle the two dynamics, as they are not mutually exclusive. On a more optimistic note, these jitters haven’t migrated to the front end of the curve. Yet. Three-year and 10-year yields are up around 50 basis points from their last auctions a month ago, hovering around 4.96% and 5.32%, respectively. The 30-year yield is up around 35 bps at 5.65%. That should be high enough to attract solid demand and ensure smooth sales, right? Probably. But if there’s a sting in the tails, volatility and uncertainty could bite across the market. Investors will be watching like, well, hawks. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. Follow ROI on LinkedIn, and X. And listen to the Morning Bid daily podcast on Apple, Spotify, or the Reuters app. Subscribe to hear Reuters journalists discuss the biggest news in markets and finance seven days a week.

item.title: Sweden to deploy Patriot missiles to NATO hub in Poland
item.description: Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said on Tuesday the Nordic country will deploy Patriot missile defence systems to eastern Poland to help protect the NATO logistics hub that supplies weapons to Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said on Tuesday the Nordic country will deploy Patriot missile defence systems to eastern Poland to help protect the NATO logistics hub that supplies weapons to Ukraine. Sweden will replace Patriot support from the Netherlands and the operation will start in December. It will deploy around 100 military personnel from the air defence unit in Halmstad, the government said Sweden [USN:L6N45M0TU TEXT:"last week announced"] that it was deploying Gripen fighter jets to Poland as part of a NATO airspace surveillance mission "The task of both the Gripen deployment and the Patriot deployment is...to protect NATO's logistics hub in Poland at the airport," Kristersson said Sweden declined to say how many Patriot system units would be sent to Poland Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk [USN:L8N4590UT TEXT:"said last month"], citing unnamed intelligence agencies, that Russia plans to launch 'hybrid' drone and missile attacks against countries supporting Ukraine Russia's President Vladimir Putin said last week that Russia had "no intention of attacking anyone...but if we are subjected to aggression, we will have no choice but to respond" (This story has been refiled to replace an incorrect image.)

item.title: Paramount wraps up mega Warner Bros merger to create Hollywood powerhouse Skydance
item.description: Paramount Skydance on Tuesday completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery , creating a Hollywood heavyweight that hands CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's largest entertainment and news businesses.
item.dc:creator: Anzar Mehraj, Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) on Tuesday completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) , creating a Hollywood heavyweight that hands CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's largest entertainment and news businesses. The deal brings together the studios behind "Mission: Impossible," "Harry Potter" and DC Studios alongside major television and streaming networks such as CBS, CNN, Paramount+ and HBO Max — forming an expansive entertainment company spanning film, TV and news. Ellison laid out his vision for the new company in a memo to employees on Tuesday in which he said the acquisition is "to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology." The goal, he added, was not simply to get bigger but "to take on the biggest players in our industry." The new company, called Skydance, is the latest iteration of a conglomerate once controlled by the late Sumner Redstone that has precipitously shrunk over the years, as audiences flock to news and entertainment delivered by a growing cadre of smaller publishers and creators chipping away at once-mighty Hollywood. Skydance not only faces competition from Netflix, Disney and others, but also from tech giants Apple, Meta, and Amazon, as well as the growing threat of AI. Shares of the combined company moved to the New York Stock Exchange from Nasdaq on Tuesday to trade under the ticker "SKYD." [USN:L4N45D11C TEXT:"Settlements"] with a [USN:L4N45D112 TEXT:"coalition of US states"] and a Hollywood writers union removed the main legal barriers to the merger, one of the largest in media history. It comes as Hollywood faces declining cable-TV subscriptions, the high cost of competing for streaming audiences and persistent pressure from unions over jobs and creative workers' rights. TRUMP'S CNN PROBLEM President Donald Trump expressed approval when asked about the deal. "It's going to be a great company," he told reporters . "That's a great merger. I'm glad they let it go." Trump has attacked news organizations since his first term and recently took the unprecedented step of [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"banning several news outlets"] from the White House, including CNN. The move came weeks ahead of the November 3 midterm elections in which Trump's fellow Republicans are defending narrow majorities in Congress. CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss [USN:L4N45R0RX TEXT:"will continue"] in their respective leadership roles in the new company and each will separately report to Ellison and Kreiz, allaying [USN:L1N42I0HA TEXT:"concerns from critics"] that Weiss, who took over as CBS News editor-in-chief in 2025, would have greater control over all of Skydance's news operations. The concerns are also fueled by [USN:L1N43G107 TEXT:"lawmakers' criticism of Ellison"] for tailoring news coverage at Paramount-owned CBS News to favor Trump. As part of the settlement, Ellison agreed to create an editorial independence board to oversee CNN and CBS. Experts warn that the board will be "[USN:L4N45E0EO TEXT:"toothless"]." Ellison [USN:L6N45R0UG TEXT:"said last week"] the Skydance name was chosen to retain the individual identities of Paramount and Warner Bros studios, rather than combining them under a new brand. Wall Street analysts, however, said the name reinforces the extent of Ellison's control, highlighting how some of Hollywood's most iconic brands now answer to him and how he has a platform to impose his strategy and culture. In just 16 years, Skydance has gone from an independent studio to the center of one of Hollywood's biggest power plays. Founded in 2010 by the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, it built its reputation as a financial backer and producer of Paramount's blockbuster "Top Gun: Maverick." After [USN:L4N3TZ1NM TEXT:"merging with"] Paramount last year, Skydance set its sights on Warner Bros, entering a heated bidding contest with Netflix (NFLX.O) while drawing interest from other potential suitors, including Comcast (CMCSA.O) . Warner Bros shareholders received an additional $41.9 million in a "ticking fee," based on the number of days between September-end and the deal-closing, according to a regulatory filing. BROADER HOLLYWOOD BET Ellison named Mattel's former CEO Ynon Kreiz as Skydance co-CEO to run day-to-day operations and lead the integration, while Ellison oversees creative direction and overall strategy. Kreiz was also appointed to the company's board on Tuesday, alongside former Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick. Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair will join the company as an adviser, it said. In bringing on Kreiz, Ellison has signaled the [USN:L4N45N0LV TEXT:"need for a cost-cutter"]. The duo faces the task of combining two large companies while delivering $6 billion in planned savings, a big part of which Paramount said would come from "non-labor sources." That includes combining technology and cloud providers of the two companies, but the scale of the cuts is expected to affect jobs across Hollywood. Skydance plans to combine its streaming services, including HBO Max and Paramount+, into a single service and has [USN:L1N45D0VR TEXT:"pledged to release at least 30 films"] each in the first two years after closing, rising to 32 a year for the following three. The combined company is also expected to carry about $80 billion in debt, putting pressure on Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cash flow from cable networks and improve theatrical film performance. Analysts at MoffettNathanson forecast profit, or EBITDA, of $16 billion for 2028 and rising to $19 billion in 2030. The research firm also predicted about $67 billion in revenue in 2028, growing to roughly $70 billion in 2030. Ellison's annual base salary will be $5 million, with a target annual bonus of $5 million, according to the filing.

item.title: Euroleague shareholders reject NBA Europe offer, door open for future talks
item.description: Europe’s biggest basketball clubs snubbed an offer to team up with the NBA on Tuesday, raising the prospect of a battle for the continent’s top teams, players and commercial riches.
item.dc:creator: Elvira Pollina
item.content:encoded: Europe’s biggest basketball clubs snubbed an offer to team up with the NBA on Tuesday, raising the prospect of a battle for the continent’s top teams, players and commercial riches. Sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters that the Euroleague's shareholder clubs rejected a collaboration offer from the NBA, though the door on a deal was not yet closed. Representatives of the 13 permanent shareholder clubs met near Lake Como, with the NBA proposal dominating discussions about the future of European basketball. In separate decisions at the meeting, the clubs agreed to convert into franchises but stopped short of formally approving an expansion of the competition from 20 to 24 teams, the Euroleague said in a statement. The move to a franchise model will give the clubs a more permanent stake in the competition than their existing long-term licences. A person attending the meeting told Reuters the decision on allocating additional long-term licences would be taken within the next month. Up to eight could be awarded and the remaining places would be filled through a combination of short-term licences, wildcards and sporting qualification through the BKT EuroCup. The Euroleague is eager to press ahead with expansion, the source said, turning attention to whether the NBA will submit a revised proposal before those decisions are made. A senior sports executive told Reuters any collaboration was unlikely to begin before 2028 because it would be difficult to organise a new competition in time for the 2027-28 season. The Euroleague did not refer to the widely reported NBA offer in its statement but told Reuters last Friday it remained open to collaboration. Although the clubs rejected the current proposal, talks with the NBA could continue. Reuters was not immediately able to confirm the details of the NBA's offer, but media reports said it envisaged the NBA's continental expansion project merging with the Euroleague. The NBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment. NBA Europe's managing director, George Aivazoglou, is due to speak at a conference in London on Thursday. FIBA, basketball's global governing body, said it would not comment at this stage. The rejection is a significant setback to efforts to combine Europe's established elite basketball competition with the financial and commercial power of the NBA, which plans to launch a 16-team NBA Europe league in 2027. SURGE OF INTEREST The NBA has stepped up its push into Europe amid a surge of interest in the sport, with Euroleague reporting in May an 82% increase in TV viewership through the first 25 regular-season rounds of the 2025-26 campaign. The NBA has also enjoyed growing momentum on the continent. Streaming deals with providers like Amazon Prime have boosted audiences for the NBA in Europe, while regular-season games in Berlin and London this year highlighted the league's growing appeal. Viewership of January's clash between Orlando Magic and Memphis Grizzlies in London was up 90% compared to the last NBA game there in 2019. A report from JB Capital commissioned by the Euroleague values the competition at €1.41 billion ($1.59 billion), while the aggregate value of its licensed teams was put at approximately €1.8 billion. Those figures pale in comparison to the NBA. The NBA recently surpassed Major League Baseball to become the world's second-richest sports league, according to Sports Value, a marketing and valuation agency, with upwards of $14 billion in revenue during the 2025-26 season. The NBA and Euroleague have said throughout this year they want to collaborate on a new competition, but both have also made clear they are prepared to pursue their own plans if no agreement is reached. They have set no formal deadline, although both sides have indicated they want greater clarity by the end of the season. The expansion drive extends the NBA's [USN:L1N3QQ016 TEXT:"longstanding effort"] towards globalisation, a trend that has emerged across North America's "Big Four" men's professional leagues, with the NFL launching a [USN:L6N44U08L TEXT:"record slate"] of nine international games this season. ($1 = 0.8883 euros)

item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

FAST

The United States has discussed starting reciprocal visits to nuclear sites with China, and plans to continue pushing in meetings in the coming months, CNN reported on Tuesday (Oct 6), citing sources familiar with the matter.

The idea of reciprocal visits was initially raised by China in meetings with US officials this year and visits to US Department of Energy national laboratories and equivalent Chinese facilities were discussed, CNN said, citing a source.

The discussions between US and Chinese officials have mainly been on the sidelines of gatherings by the UN Security Council's five veto-wielding permanent members, CNN reported.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The White House and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours.

US President Donald Trump called for trilateral arms control negotiations between the US, China and Russia when he met President Xi Jinping last month. However, the two leaders did not discuss the possibility of nuclear site visits during their talks, the CNN report said, citing a US official.

Beijing has said its nuclear arsenal is far smaller than those of Russia and the US, something it says makes its participation in such talks unnecessary.

Another meeting between Trump and Xi is widely considered likely this year, potentially at November's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China or during Group of 20 meetings in the US in December.

By the time the two leaders meet again, it is expected that further lower-level discussions on possible nuclear site visits will have taken place, CNN said.

Related:

Five takeaways from Trump's summit with Xi in Washington

Highlights: Trump hails 'tremendous strides' and Xi calls for 'healthy' competition as leaders meet

Source: Reuters/ia

item.title: Rubio tells Russia to share more information about plague death
item.description: Russia should share more information about the death of a plague laboratory worker who died last week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday, in an incident Washington was watching "very closely".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia should share more information about the death of a [USN:S8N45F09U TEXT:"plague laboratory worker"] who died last week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday, in an incident Washington was watching "very closely". A laboratory worker at Siberia's plague research institute fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Friday, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people and sparking public health fears on social media. Russian authorities have said the situation is under control. "I think it's incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world," Rubio told reporters in Iceland. "We're watching it very closely, hour by hour." Rubio said the US has measures available to help Russia if the situation turns out to be more serious than has so far been acknowledged, but needed to know more before it could step in. President Donald Trump told reporters on Tuesday he had a call scheduled very soon with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. When asked what intelligence agencies were saying about the situation in Russia, Trump replied: "So far we are in very deep discussions, we'll be able to report about it probably tomorrow."
